sections.h2: How does Panama City's bay location shape a house sale?
sections.html:
Panama City sits on St. Andrews Bay in the Florida Panhandle, about 170 miles east of Mobile, 95 miles east of Pensacola and 100 miles southwest of Tallahassee. The bay wraps much of the city and shelters the harbor of the Port of Panama City complex.

The city's own climate summary gives an annual average of 68.8 degrees, a summer average of 89 and a winter average of 64, and 57.86 inches of rain and other precipitation in an average year, per the city. Winds run mostly southerly in summer and north to northwesterly in winter. Moisture and salt air shape what buyers inspect first: roofs, window seals, siding and anything near the water.

Bay County also tells residents to look up their address on its evacuation zone map, and notes that the zones may differ from what people assume. A seller who knows the zone and the FEMA flood map status of the lot can answer the questions that insurers and buyers raise early.

The county's floodplain ordinance was updated to federally required standards, with new flood maps taking effect on August 16 of the year the commission adopted them, and the county posts a static copy of the updated flood zones in its map gallery. Because of that, ask which map your parcel sits on before you describe flood risk to a buyer.

sections.h2: Which parts of town do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
The water is the draw. The city lists public boat ramps at St. Andrews Marina, Downtown Marina, Carl Gray Park, Snug Harbor and Bob George Park. Waterfront parks include Adams, Asbell, Calhoun Beach, Millville Waterfront, Oaks by the Bay and Venetian Sunset, plus the Lake Huntington Clubhouse.

  • St. Andrews, Downtown and Millville are tied together by a mural trail with more than 15 exhibits.
  • Downtown holds the Center for the Arts, and the Martin Theatre is described as upcoming.
  • Two city marinas on the Intracoastal Waterway take vessels up to 130 feet.

Recreation counts on the city page run to eight walking trails, 13 playgrounds, four tennis courts, four pickleball courts, eight baseball fields, five softball fields, 20 multipurpose fields, a dog park, a skate park and a disc golf course, with a recreation center listed as coming. Give your distance to any of these in plain miles, since a buyer will check it on a map.

sections.h2: What do museums, festivals and schools add to a listing?
sections.html:
Arts events give a lifestyle angle. The city names the Red Fish Film Festival, FLLUXE and the Public Eye SOAR projection festival, along with the Science & Discovery Center of Northwest Florida and the Bay County Historical Museum.

Local arts groups include the Panama City Symphony Orchestra, Kaleidoscope Theatre, the Gulf Jazz Society and the Panama City Ballet. Residents cite pleasant weather, housing choice, fishing and water sports and a small-town feel as reasons they live here, according to the city's own page.

Bay County's website also notes a half-cent surtax funding road and utility projects, with an interactive project map. A seller can point a buyer there instead of guessing which streets are slated for work.

sections.h2: What permit history should a Panama City seller pull?
sections.html:
Pull every permit, final inspection and certificate for work done on the house. The city requires a permit before a project starts, including reroofing, decks, carports, sheds, remodels and changes to electrical, plumbing, mechanical, structural, irrigation or insulation systems.

The duty to confirm permits rests on the owner or the owner's authorized agent. A permit goes invalid if work does not begin within 6 months of issuance or stops for 6 months after it starts, and an extension must be requested in writing with a fee. Work has to stay exposed for inspection until approved.

The city issues a certificate of occupancy for a structure and a certificate of completion where occupancy does not apply, such as a reroof or system alteration. Building Services is at 501 Harrison Ave., phone 850-872-3025. Some projects need approval from other agencies too; the city names the Florida Department of Environmental Protection as an example.

sections.h2: How do Bay County tax dates and discounts work for a seller?
sections.html:
Notices are normally mailed on or before November 1 with a due date of March 31, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1. Discounts shrink month by month.

Non-ad valorem charges for paving, stormwater and solid waste ride on the same bill and also become delinquent April 1. The collector says changes to a name, address, location or assessed value go through the property appraiser, and that an escrow servicer should request the original notice so the owner gets a copy.

sections.h2: Where can I pay or ask questions in person?
sections.html:
The Bay County Tax Collector runs offices in Panama City at 850 W. 11th St., Panama City Beach at 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Lynn Haven at 700 Florida Ave. and Callaway at 805 S. Tyndall Pkwy. Renewal kiosks sit inside the Publix stores on W. 23rd St. and on Panama City Beach Parkway.

  • Bring the tax notice or the property address; only Bay County property tax is taken at these counters.
  • Delinquent payments must be made with certified funds: cash, cashier's check, money order or card.
  • Appointments can be booked online for each office.

sections.h2: Does homestead stay with a Panama City house after a sale?
sections.html:
No. The exemption belongs to the resident owner, and a sale lifts the capped assessment back to full market-based value at the next year's start, so a buyer can open with a bigger bill than yours.

A permanent home can lose up to $50,000 of taxable value, with school taxes touched only by the first $25,000. The Bay County property appraiser takes applications until March 1. Moving within Florida? Portability can carry your capped savings to the next house, provided you set up that homestead inside three years.

Bay County's site described Amendment 3, a constitutional change on the November 3, 2026 ballot that would raise the non-school homestead exemption if 60 percent of voters approved. Ask the property appraiser what the final outcome means for your parcel.

Bay County also requires registration, reporting and inspection for vacation rentals in the unincorporated areas, a detail worth knowing if your house has been used for short stays and the new owner wants to continue.

sections.h2: What do deed charges look like at a Bay County closing?
sections.html:
Florida's deed tax is seventy cents per hundred dollars of price, and all parties to the deed stay liable for it. The clerk takes it at recording.

Recording fees open at five dollars for page one and four dollars for every later page, then add a trust fund charge and a technology charge per page. A mortgage the buyer assumes counts toward the consideration, so the closing agent adds it to the total.

sections.h2: What if the Panama City house is inherited, rented or behind on taxes?
sections.html:
Each case has its own clock. Florida offers a shortcut for modest estates and a short written demand for unpaid rent, so ask a lawyer which route fits.

If tax stays unpaid, the county sells a certificate against the parcel and an investor can eventually seek a tax deed, which is why a payoff matters. Collect the payoff letter, the lease or the court file before you weigh an offer.

faqs.q: What is the climate like in Panama City?
faqs.a: The city reports an annual average of 68.8 degrees, a summer average of 89 and a winter average of 64, with 57.86 inches of precipitation yearly.

faqs.q: When are Bay County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Notices go out on or before November 1 with a due date of March 31. Taxes unpaid after that become delinquent on April 1.

faqs.q: Which permits should I check before selling in Panama City?
faqs.a: Check permits for roofs, decks, sheds, remodels and electrical, plumbing, mechanical and structural work, plus any certificate of occupancy or completion. Call Building Services at 850-872-3025.

faqs.q: Does the Bay County Tax Collector have an office on Panama City Beach?
faqs.a: Yes. It lists an office at 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Panama City Beach, along with offices in Panama City, Lynn Haven and Callaway.

faqs.q: Can homestead carry over to a house I buy next?
faqs.a: Partly. Portability can transfer the Save Our Homes difference to a new Florida homestead if you establish it within three years, and you file for it with the new county's property appraiser.
